title: Failover fuzzing harness for SLO-driven multi-region failover, GPU pressure, and load-shedding
creator: Diego Ramirez
description: Create a repeatable, automated chaos/fuzzing harness that exercises multi-region failover, GPU pool exhaustion, and downstream dependency blackholes to validate SLOs, circuit breaker behavior, and load-shedding policies. The harness should be usable in CI and ad-hoc experiments, produce traceable metrics, and drive alerting/Runbook improvements. Goal: surface edge cases where automatic failovers or shedding lead to quality regressions or customer-visible latency/cost spikes.
tasks: Design harness API for injection scenarios (region down, full GPU pool, dependency blackhole, latency spike)
Implement simulation layer that can instruct routing service to mark a region as unreachable
Add GPU pressure simulator that limits available GPU tokens and reports pool exhaustion events
Wire the harness to the runtime's circuit-breaker toggles and routing policies
Produce standardized output (JSON) with per-run metrics: error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-second, fallback rate
Integrate with existing chaos dashboard and add experiment summary ribbons
Create CI job that runs lightweight scenario matrix on every canary of routing or circuit-breaker changes
Author Runbook updates for detected failure modes and rollback criteria
acceptance_criteria: Harness can trigger and recover from a simulated single-region outage with automated verification of failover within configured RTO
GPU exhaustion scenario causes expected shedding behavior (queueing limits or rejects) and does not violate p95 latency SLO more than agreed threshold
Dependency blackhole scenario flips circuit breakers and records fallback counts in the console dashboard
All scenarios emit structured JSON artifacts and traces that link to request IDs for post-run analysis
CI job runs the core three scenarios (region outage, GPU pressure, dependency blackhole) in under 20m and fails the pipeline if regressions exceed thresholds
Runbook updated with reproduction steps, key dashboards, and escalation page
testing_plan: Phase A (dev): local run using dev-control-plane, lightweight injection that toggles the router weight to 0 for a region
Phase B (staging): run full harness against staging Dedicated cluster with observability enabled, collect traces and SLI deltas
Phase C (canary): include harness in pre-release CI for routing and circuit-breaker changes; run limited scenario set
Phase D (post-release): scheduled monthly chaos run against non-prod replicas and quarterly run against a copy of production traffic (blue/green tape) with legal/compliance signoff
notes_or_updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff — defined scope and high-level API. PM wants measurable SLI deltas per-run.

2026-02-20: Prototype of region toggle completed (Morgan Chen) — uses routing policy override in the control plane. Observed immediate 10% increase in p95 for cross-region calls during naive failover.
2026-02-24: Discovered that KV cache warmup after failover contributes 40% of tail latency; added metric to track cache miss rate per-population. Decision: add warmup window to SLA evaluation.

2026-02-27: GPU pressure simulator implemented (Asha) as token bucket limiter that can simulate node-level OOM by returning 503s when exhausted. Early runs show client-side retry backoff amplifies load; need to validate client retry guards.
2026-03-01: Design review with PM and SRE: prefer opt-in chaos gating in CI and require 'chaos-accept' flag for scheduled runs against staging. Action: add gating flag to pipeline and update docs.
2026-03-02: Added tracing hook to attach experiment-id to all spawned requests so postmortem queries are easier; created PR #1042
review_feedback: PM (Morgan Chen): Ensure experiment output includes 'quality-of-output' checks for sampling model responses — not just latency/errors.
SRE (Yuki Tanaka): Add a 'blast radius' parameter so we can run node-only vs region-wide experiments.
Runtime Eng (Luis Herrera): For GPU exhaustion, prefer to simulate via admission control rather than OOM to avoid real node instability in staging.
decisions: Use routing policy override (control plane) for region simulation to avoid touching the underlying infra network layer.
Simulate GPU pool exhaustion at the admission layer by refusing new inferences when token bucket drained (safer for staging).
Emit experiment-id in traces and structured logs for all injected runs to simplify correlation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Chaos runs could accidentally escalate to production and cause customer impact. Mitigation: require explicit 'chaos-accept' flag and RBAC gating; keep experiments limited to staging by default.

Risk: Client-side retries can amplify load leading to cascading failures. Mitigation: add synthetic clients that mimic bounded retry policies and verify amplification effects; add telemetry showing retry amplification ratio.
Risk: Warm cache penalty skews SLO results. Mitigation: measure cache-warmup separately and exclude first X minutes from regression gating or include warmup behavior as an SLO dimension.
rollout_plan: Merge harness to main behind feature flag.
Run full harness in staging for 48h and collect metrics.
Introduce CI job for core scenarios on every PR touching routing/circuit-breaker code paths.
Announce to engineering and SRE teams with instructions and opt-in form for scheduled blue-green production shadow run.
followups: ENG-8429: Add quality-of-output sampling into harness to detect hallucination/regression under failover
ENG-8430: Implement client retry guard library used by SDKs to limit amplification on failures
PM-421: Update SLOs to include multi-region failover RTO and warmup window definitions
